# harsat

## What is HARSAT?

HARSAT (Harmonised Regional Seas Assessment Tool), is a tool that is
applied by The Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme (AMAP), the
Helsinki Commission (HELCOM) and the OSPAR Commission (OSPAR) to support
their assessments of data concerning contaminants (hazardous substances)
and their effects in the marine environment.

HARSAT code includes tools for pre-processing data, statistical trend
analysis and comparison with threshold values, and post-processing for
archiving and reporting.

HARSAT is developed in the statistical computing language R. R is
available for most operating systems and can be downloaded from the
R-project website.

Disclaimer: The HARSAT tool is made available under an Open Source
licence. While every attempt has been made to ensure that the HARSAT
version(s) developed and supported by AMAP/HELCOM/OSPAR are free of
errors, any use of the tool by third parties, and the quality of
products of third party use is the responsibility of the third party
concerned.

## System requirements

- R programming language (version 4.2.1 or later). Additional R packages
  to those which come with the standard R installation may be needed –
  they will normally be installed automatically, but you may need
  permissions or tools to do this
- R Studio (recommended; version 2023.03.1 or later). While not
  required, the HARSAT developers recommend running the HARSAT code
  using the RStudio integrated development environment.

## Installation

For full installation details, see the [Getting
Started](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/harsat.md) guide. We
recommend installing `harsat` from a packaged bundle, either using
RStudio or the R command line, as this ensures that all dependencies are
up-to-date, properly downloaded and installed.

### In RStudio

To do this, you will need a downloaded package bundle, typically a file
called something like `harsat_0.1.2.tar.gz`.

From the `Packages` tab, choose `Install`, make sure you have selected
to install from a Package Archive File, then press the `Browse...`
button and locate your bundled package file. Then finally press the
`Install` button.

### From the R command line

To do this, you will need a downloaded package bundle, typically a file
called something like `harsat_0.1.2.tar.gz`.

In the R command line, use a command (passing the filename of wherever
you have downloaded the file to):

``` r
install.packages(remotes) -- if needed
library(remotes)
remotes::install_local("~/Downloads/harsat_0.1.2.tar")
```

### Directly from Github

Alternatively, you can also install `harsat` directly from GitHub.

``` r

library(remotes)
remotes::install_github("osparcomm/HARSAT@main")
```

The development version is similar, but changes more often, so we only
recommend this if you enjoy a more exciting time for your analysis.

``` r

library(remotes)
remotes::install_github("osparcomm/HARSAT@develop")
```

## Example usage

We have prepared zip files containing all the other files you need, for
both OSPAR (a subset of OSPAR 2022), and HELCOM (based on HELCOM 2023).
These zip files contain two directories: a data directory and an
information directory. You can unzip these anywhere you like on your
system.

- [Download the OSPAR
  archive](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/ospar.zip)
- [Download the HELCOM
  archive](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/helcom.zip)
- [Download the external data (AMAP)
  archive](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/external.zip)

Let’s say you have unzipped these to a file on your system, such as
`C:\Users\test\ospar`. So, the data is now in
`C:\Users\test\ospar\data`, and the reference files are in
`C:\Users\test\ospar\information`, although can rename and move these
anywhere you like.

To read the data, you will then do something like this (we’re using
water in OSPAR as an example here – for the complete example, have a
look at [the full OSPAR
example](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/example_OSPAR.md)):

``` r

water_data <- read_data(
  compartment = "water", 
  purpose = "OSPAR",                               
  contaminants = "water.txt", 
  stations = "stations.txt", 
  data_dir = file.path("C:", "users", "test", "ospar", "data"),         ## i.e., C:\Users\test\ospar\data
  info_dir = file.path("C:", "users", "test", "ospar", "information"),  ## i.e., C:\Users\test\ospar\information
  extraction = "2023/08/23"
)
```

And follow the rest of the process as shown in the [Getting Started
guide](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/harsat.md) or the
[OSPAR
example](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/example_OSPAR.md).

You can, of course, start to edit the files in these directories as you
choose. Note that there are some specific naming conventions for the
files in the reference file directory especially. Find out more in [the
documentation page for file
management](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/file-management.md).

## More information

For more information, take a look at the [Getting Started
guide](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/articles/harsat.md).

We welcome any other contributions you can make. Check out the
[Contributor’s guide](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for more.

# Package index

## Primary functions

These are the functions you’re likely to need for any assessment. For
most standard assessments, these will be all you need.

- [`read_data()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/read_data.md)
  : Read HARSAT data
- [`tidy_data()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/tidy_data.md)
  : Tidy the data
- [`create_timeseries()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/create_timeseries.md)
  : Create a time series
- [`run_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/run_assessment.md)
  : Assess timeseries for trends and status
- [`update_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/update_assessment.md)
  : Update timeseries assessments
- [`check_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/check_assessment.md)
  : Check whether the assessments have converged
- [`write_summary_table()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/write_summary_table.md)
  : Write assessment summary to a csv file
- [`plot_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/plot_assessment.md)
  : Graphical summaries of an assessment
- [`report_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/report_assessment.md)
  : Reports the assessment of individual time series

## All functions

- [`add_stations()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/add_stations.md)
  : Add stations to contaminant data from an ICES extraction

- [`apply_subset()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/apply_subset.md)
  : Apply subsetting to a time series

- [`check_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/check_assessment.md)
  : Check whether the assessments have converged

- [`check_convergence_lmm()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/check_convergence_lmm.md)
  : Checks convergence of an assessment model

- [`convert_reftable()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/convert_reftable.md)
  : Add OSPAR_subregion to simplified sediment threshold reference table

- [`convert_units()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/convert_units.md)
  : Converts units, e.g., from mg/kg to ug/kg

- [`create_timeseries()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/create_timeseries.md)
  : Create a time series

- [`cstm.VDS.environment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/cstm.VDS.environment.md)
  : Detects the environment from the call

- [`ctsm.VDS.loglik.calc()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm.VDS.loglik.calc.md)
  : ctsm.VDS.loglik.calc

- [`ctsm.VDS.p.calc()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm.VDS.p.calc.md)
  : ctsm.VDS.p.calc

- [`ctsm.VDS.varlist`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm.VDS.varlist.md)
  : ctsm.VDS.varlist

- [`ctsm.projection()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm.projection.md)
  : Calculates a polar projection

- [`ctsm_TBT_convert()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm_TBT_convert.md)
  : Convert tin concentrations

- [`ctsm_convert_basis()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm_convert_basis.md)
  : Basis and matrix information and basis conversion

- [`ctsm_get_determinands()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm_get_determinands.md)
  : Get the determinands to be assessed

- [`ctsm_get_info()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm_get_info.md)
  : Gets data from the standard reference tables

- [`ctsm_uncrt_plot_data()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ctsm_uncrt_plot_data.md)
  : Generates a relative uncertainty plot

- [`get_AC`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_AC.md) :
  Access function map

- [`get_AC_biota_OSPAR()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_AC_biota_OSPAR.md)
  : Gets OSPAR threshold values for biota

- [`get_basis_biota_OSPAR()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_basis_biota_OSPAR.md)
  : Gets the OSPAR biota target basis

- [`get_basis_default()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_basis_default.md)
  : The default function for generating a basis

- [`get_station_code()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_station_code.md)
  : Get station code from station name

- [`get_timeseries()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/get_timeseries.md)
  : Extracts timeSeries

- [`harsat`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/harsat-package.md)
  [`harsat-package`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/harsat-package.md)
  : harsat: Harmonized Regional Seas Assessment Tool

- [`` `$` ``](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/info_TEF.md) :
  TEFs for selected groups of compounds

- [`label_normaliser()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/label_normaliser.md)
  : Text representation of normaliser information for plots and reports

- [`label_unit()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/label_unit.md)
  : Text representation of units for plots and reports

- [`locate_information_file()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/locate_information_file.md)
  : Find the path for an information file

- [`make_key()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/make_key.md)
  : Make key for annotating assessment plots

- [`normalise_biota_HELCOM()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/normalise_biota_HELCOM.md)
  : Normalises biota concentrations, HELCOM vwersion

- [`normalise_sediment_HELCOM()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/normalise_sediment_HELCOM.md)
  : Normalises sediment concentrations, HELCOM version

- [`normalise_sediment_OSPAR()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/normalise_sediment_OSPAR.md)
  : Normalises sediment concentrations, OSPAR version

- [`ordinal_theta_cl()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ordinal_theta_cl.md)
  : Calculates confidence limits for imposex time series

- [`ordinal_theta_est()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/ordinal_theta_est.md)
  : Estimates cut-points in ordinal model (imposex assessments)

- [`parallel_objects()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/parallel_objects.md)
  :

  Identifies functions needed for parallel processing in
  `run_assessment`

- [`plot_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/plot_assessment.md)
  : Graphical summaries of an assessment

- [`pretty_unit()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/pretty_unit.md)
  : Pretty representation of units for plots and reports

- [`read_ICES_file()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/read_ICES_file.md)
  : Reads an ICES extraction

- [`read_contaminants()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/read_contaminants.md)
  : Reads contaminant data

- [`read_data()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/read_data.md)
  : Read HARSAT data

- [`read_stations()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/read_stations.md)
  : Reads station dictionary

- [`report_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/report_assessment.md)
  : Reports the assessment of individual time series

- [`report_file_digest()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/report_file_digest.md)
  : Generates and logs a file digest

- [`run_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/run_assessment.md)
  : Assess timeseries for trends and status

- [`run_control_default()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/run_control_default.md)
  **\[experimental\]** :

  Default control parameters for `run_assessment`

- [`run_control_modify()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/run_control_modify.md)
  :

  Modifies control parameters for `run_assessment`

- [`safe_read_file()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/safe_read_file.md)
  : Reads an input file, given a particular encoding, and possibly
  additional hints

- [`subset_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/subset_assessment.md)
  : Subsets an assessment object

- [`tidy_data()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/tidy_data.md)
  : Tidy the data

- [`update_assessment()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/update_assessment.md)
  : Update timeseries assessments

- [`write_summary_table()`](http://osparcomm.github.io/HARSAT/reference/write_summary_table.md)
  : Write assessment summary to a csv file
